findings.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so the slot's end is never actually validated against the working-hours window. `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` equals `start`, so the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` reduces to `start > workingHour.endTime`: a 60-minute slot that starts at 16:30 against working hours ending 17:00 passes the check, and a slot that starts before workingHour.startTime is correctly blocked but the end-side boundary check is dead code — slots that overhang the end of working hours are returned as available.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with strict identity, which is always false. The intended zero-length/unavailable-all-day override branch never executes; a date override whose start equals its end is treated as a normal range and the day-level 'dateOverrideExist' fallthrough at line 116 wrongly returns true (available) for every slot that day, exposing slots the organizer explicitly marked unavailable.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called on a field the type declares as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and no producer of the `activeOverrides` passed into `getSlots` is shown to populate it, so `dayjs().tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's local timezone. When `override.timeZone` is undefined, `organizerUtcOffset` becomes the server machine's UTC offset instead of the organizer's, producing a wrong `offset` and thus wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes that unsets the wrong working-hours rows — availability is corrupted for any getSlots call site that doesn't thread timeZone through (the diff only adds timeZone on the dateOverrides in viewer/slots.ts getSchedule, a different object graph).

[BUG] `userSchedule?.timeZone` yields `undefined` when the slot's `slotUserId` has no matching entry in `userAvailability`, and `checkIfIsAvailable` then takes the `organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0` branch, computing a zero utcOffset. For round-robin slots whose userId isn't found in `userAvailability`, the date-override day comparison uses `format("YYYY MM DD")` on the raw UTC instant, matching the override to the wrong calendar day and filtering slots in/out incorrectly across timezone boundaries.

[BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is inside the override window, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before reaching the busy-events check, so conflicts are never consulted. A user who has a confirmed booking or calendar-busy event that overlaps the override window still sees those slots as bookable in getSchedule, and can book a double-booking; the busy.every() conflict logic below is silently skipped for every overridden day.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime (identical to `start`) instead of the slot's end time, and drops seconds, so it reads `const start = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. A slot that starts at 16:45 with a 30-minute event length passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test even though it ends at 17:15 past a 17:00 working-hours end, so getSchedule returns slots that extend beyond working hours; the check can never test anything start doesn't already test.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs wrapper objects with strict equality, which is always false. The zero-length-override early-return branch is dead code, so a zero-length (unavailable/blocked) date override falls through to the time comparisons and can be treated as an available window instead of a block, exposing slots the organizer explicitly blocked.

[BUG] The override comparison mixes clock domains: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` yields the organizer's local wall time while `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime` are UTC wall times, so the two sides differ by the organizer's UTC offset for any non-UTC organizer. For an organizer in +5:30, an override stored as 18:00–22:00 UTC is compared against slots as if it were 12:30–17:00 UTC; slots are wrongly excluded from and wrongly included in the override window, so the PR's own timezone-fix goal fails for every non-UTC organizer.

[BUG] The new offset math computes minutes-of-day via `.hour()*60 + .minute()` after shifting by the invitee offset, so an override that crosses midnight in the invitee's timezone produces startTime/endTime values outside 0–1439 (or wrapped), which the downstream unset loop matching overrides against working-hours minute ranges cannot handle. An organizer override of 22:00–02:00 viewed by an invitee 6 hours ahead becomes a 04:00–08:00 window computed on the wrong day, and working hours for the intended day are unset based on the wrong date, producing wrong availability for multi-day windows around the override.

[ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` dereferences `override.timeZone`, which the diff itself types as optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts (`timeZone?: string`), and serializes a Date through toString() before re-parsing. Any producer of TimeRange/dateOverrides that does not populate timeZone (the type contract permits it) gets `dayjs.tz(undefined)` — the current instant — so the offset is computed for 'now' rather than the override date, silently mis-shifting DST-sensitive overrides; a future maintainer cannot tell which producers guarantee the field.

[ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff exercises the getSchedule happy path for one extra invitee timezone, while the entirely new logic in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable (dateOverrideExist gating, the working-hours check, the organizerTimeZone shift) has no test anywhere in the diff. A regression in checkIfIsAvailable — such as the end-time and busy-check defects present in this very diff — ships undetected; the next change to slot filtering has no safety net, and reviewers cannot verify the new working-hours branch behaves correctly for any timezone or busy-overlap case.

[BUG] The new working-hours check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime`, so the working-hours end bound is never enforced. `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` should derive from `slotEndTime`; any slot that starts before `workingHour.endTime` but runs past close of business is returned as available, e.g. a 60-minute event whose slot starts at 16:30 against a 17:00 end is offered even though it ends at 17:30.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object identity of two distinct Dayjs instances, so it is always false. The intended zero-length-override short-circuit (treat override as full-day/unblock) never fires; a zero-length date override that should make the day available instead falls through to the start/end comparisons, where `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` returns true and the day is silently filtered out — the exact opposite of the intended behavior.

[BUG] The organizer offset is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, which both parses a Date with tz() incorrectly and inverts the sign of utcOffset. `dayjs.tz(dateObj, tz)` re-interprets the Date's local wall time in `organizerTimeZone` rather than converting it, and then multiplying `utcOffset()` by -1 flips the offset direction; for any organizer east of UTC the override's calendar day comparison `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format(...)` matches the wrong day, so date overrides block or free the wrong dates for non-UTC organizers.

[ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable re-implements date-override and working-hours filtering from scratch, duplicating the existing enforcement in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots, and the two implementations already disagree in mechanism (slots.ts shifts override times by the invitee-vs-organizer offset; this code shifts by an inverted organizer offset and compares formatted day strings). There are now two hand-maintained sources of truth for the same availability invariant on the same request path; the next maintainer changing override semantics must update both or slots produced by getSlots will be silently filtered differently by checkIfIsAvailable — the divergence is already present in this diff.

[BUG] The override-window checks reject a slot only if `slotEndTime` is at/before the override start or `slotStartTime` is after the override end, but accept slots that straddle the override boundary (start before the override begins, end inside it), and since `dateOverrideExist` then returns true unconditionally, such slots bypass working-hours checks entirely. A slot overlapping the edge of a date override (e.g. starting 30 minutes before the override window) is returned as available even though part of the booking falls outside the override's permitted window and outside normal working hours.

[ADVISORY] The diff hoists `organizerTimeZone` computation out of the loop and then, for round-robin/collective hosts, overrides it per-user via `userSchedule?.timeZone`, but for fixed events passes `schedule.timeZone` — the availability check receives a timezone whose semantics differ per code path with no single traceable requirement for which one governs. A future change to how eventType-level vs user-level timezones resolve (e.g. schedule-less event types) will produce different override filtering for fixed vs round-robin event types from the same PR-added code, and maintainers must reason about three assignment sites (lines ~439, ~492, ~517, ~579) to change it safely.

[BUG] In the new workingHours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `end` is computed from slotStartTime (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) instead of slotEndTime, so start === end and the `end > workingHour.endTime` test degenerates to a start-time comparison. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past workingHour.endTime is wrongly marked available — e.g. a 60-minute slot at 16:30 against a 17:00 working-hours end slips through the availability check and is shown as bookable; the intended `end` must come from slotEndTime.

[BUG] The new workingHours gate compares UTC components of the slot against organizer-local working-hour values: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` so `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + minute()` is UTC minutes, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes in the organizer's timezone, and `slotStartTime.day()` is the UTC weekday while `workingHour.days` holds local weekdays. For any organizer not on UTC (e.g. +6:00 with 09:00-17:00 working hours), the check filters the wrong slots — slots near local boundaries are rejected or admitted incorrectly, and slots on the local Sunday/Saturday boundary are evaluated against the wrong day. This gate also duplicates the working-hours filtering already done in getSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts), creating two parallel filter paths that can disagree.

[BUG] The full-day-override test `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs wrapper objects with strict reference equality, which is always false. The full-day (start==end) date-override branch is dead code and never fires; the code falls through to the before/after checks instead, which for a start==end override reject every slot that isn't strictly after the override instant — i.e. full-day overrides behave as point overrides and slots that should be available are marked unavailable (or vice versa) depending on the subsequent branches.

[BUG] The offset correction shifts only the time-of-day of each override (`dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`) while the day-matching loop immediately below still keys off the original, unshifted override window, so when the offset pushes the override across midnight (offsets > the override's distance from 00:00) the shifted startTime is larger than endTime and the unset loop subtracts shifted times against an unshifted day. For organizer/invitee timezone pairs whose offset crosses a midnight boundary (e.g. organizer at +6:00 with an 00:00-08:00 override viewed from UTC-8), the computed startTime > endTime and the working-hours-unset loop removes the wrong (or no) hours, producing slots outside the override window or hiding the override entirely.

[ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the newly-optional `timeZone` field on TimeRange; any caller building dateOverrides without setting timeZone (the field was just made optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts) passes undefined into dayjs.tz, and the offset then defaults to the host machine's timezone rather than failing loudly. Server operators on hosts whose local tz differs from the organizer's get silently wrong override windows; the field should be required or the missing case should throw rather than degrade to server-local offsets.

[ADVISORY] The `organizerTimeZone` fallback chain ends with `userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone`, i.e. the timezone of whichever availability record happened to be first, not necessarily the organizer's. When eventType.timeZone and schedule.timeZone are unset (collective/round-robin setups), availability math silently keys off an arbitrary member's timezone; results shift per query depending on Prisma row order.

[ADVISORY] In the round-robin branch, `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(...)` can return undefined (userId not found among availability), and `userSchedule?.timeZone` then yields undefined organizerTimeZone, which checkIfIsAvailable treats as utcOffset 0 instead of the real organizer offset. For a slot userId missing from userAvailability, the date-override date comparison silently runs as if the organizer were on UTC, admitting/rejecting slots against the wrong day.

[ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` is recomputed twice per boundary (four dayjs constructions per override) instead of computing the shifted start/end once. Pure wasted allocation on the hot slots path with no behavior benefit; a single `const shiftedStart = ...; const shiftedEnd = ...` halves the work and removes the risk of the four copies drifting apart.

[BUG] When a slot falls inside a date override's day and passes the range checks, `dateOverrideExist` causes `checkIfIsAvailable` to `return true` before the `busy.every(...)` check ever runs. Slots during a date override are offered even when the host has a confirmed booking or busy block overlapping them, so users can book double-booked times — the function's original purpose (busy filtering) is silently bypassed whenever an override exists.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — identical to `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never fire, so slots that start inside working hours but extend past closing time (e.g. a 60-min slot at 16:45 with endTime 17:00) are accepted as available and bookable past the host's working window.

[BUG] The working-hours comparison mixes UTC slot minutes with organizer-local working-hour minutes: `slotStartTime` is `.utc()` (per line `const slotStartTime = time.utc();`) while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes-from-midnight in the organizer's timezone, with no offset applied. For any host whose timezone is not UTC, valid slots inside working hours are rejected and slots outside working hours are accepted — availability is shifted by the host's UTC offset.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two Dayjs object instances by reference, which is always false regardless of values. The intended zero-length-override case is never detected, so a zero-length/unavailability override never short-circuits the range logic as designed; the branch is dead code.

[BUG] The `organizerTimeZone` argument is passed as `schedule.timeZone` — the invitee's schedule timezone from the per-slot schedule lookup — while the parameter was explicitly introduced as the organizer's timezone. The date-override day-matching in `checkIfIsAvailable` (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`) uses the wrong party's timezone, so for invitee and organizer in different timezones the override's date boundaries are computed incorrectly and slots are wrongly included/excluded; the same intent inversion occurs at the loose-host path (line ~514, `userSchedule.timeZone`) which passes the attendee user's timezone.

[ADVISORY] `getSlots` now shifts override start/end by the invitee-minus-organizer offset, changing the semantics of `startTime`/`endTime` from organizer-local (UTC-extracted) minutes to invitee-local minutes, while the surrounding loop (`start = 0; start < 1440`) still assumes organizer-local day framing. The next maintainer of the working-hours-unsetting loop will reason about the old semantics; after an offset shift an override near midnight can wrap past 1440 or below 0 and the loop silently misses it, leaving conflicting working hours un-removed for cross-timezone host/invitee pairs.

[BUG] The full-day-override check compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false because dayjs returns new object instances. A date override intended to block an entire day (start === end, i.e. an unavailable/unbookable day set by the organizer) is never detected as a blocker; dateOverrideExist is set true and the function returns true (slot available), so users can book on days the organizer explicitly blocked.

[BUG] In the working-hours check, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` uses the slot's own start time instead of the slot's end time, so both start and end are the same value. The `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never fire for a slot whose start is within hours but whose end extends past workingHours.endTime (it only fires when the start itself is past the end of hours, identical to the first condition); slots that overrun the organizer's working hours are returned as available, letting users book past closing time.

[BUG] When a slot's date matches a date-override day but the slot falls outside the override window, the function's control flow marks dateOverrideExist and skips the working-hours rejection for other days' logic, and `dateOverrides.find(...)` returning undefined still leaves dateOverrideExist true causing `return true` for slots on the override day that begin before the override start. On a day with a partial override (e.g. 09:00–12:00), any slot whose date matches the override day but whose slotEndTime is after the override start passes the two early `return true` paths inside find() only when slotEndTime <= overrideStart; slots overlapping or inside the window fall through the find, but the subsequent `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` unconditionally returns available for slots that are on the override day at all, so slots inside the excluded override window are treated as bookable when the author intended the opposite polarity.

[BUG] The all-day-override check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two dayjs wrapper objects with strict identity equality, which is never true, so the zero-length (all-day) override branch is dead code. An all-day date override (start === end) is never detected as covering the whole day, so slots on that day fall through to the partial-window comparisons and can be wrongly rejected or wrongly accepted depending on the slot time; no test in the diff exercises a zero-length override, so this regression ships silently.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of the slot's end time, so a slot that starts within working hours but ends after workingHours.endTime is never rejected. Slots that overrun the end of a working day pass the availability check and are offered to bookers even though the host is unavailable for the full slot duration — e.g. a 60-minute slot starting at endTime-30min is returned as available; the new workingHours branch has zero test coverage, so nothing in the suite catches it.

[BUG] When dateOverrideExist is true but the find callback returned undefined (slot overlaps the override window), the function hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` and skips the `busy.every(...)` check entirely, so slots within a date override bypass all busy-time validation. A slot that falls inside a date override is marked available even when a confirmed booking (busy entry) overlaps it, enabling double-booking; no test in the diff combines a date override with an overlapping booking.

[ADVISORY] The single test added in this diff only exercises the getSlots date-override timezone-offset path in packages/lib/slots.ts, leaving both new branches in checkIfIsAvailable (the dateOverride existence logic and the workingHours rejection logic, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts lines ~103-152) with zero test coverage — the only test-shaped file changed is apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts, and its new case asserts slot times without any assertion touching the new workingHours/dateOverride filtering in checkIfIsAvailable. Future changes to the new checkIfIsAvailable branches (which the identified start/end and busy-bypass bugs already show to be wrong) will pass the entire suite, so the next maintainer gets false green CI when this diff's actual behavior is broken.

[ADVISORY] The new test's expected slot list is asserted to be identical to the previous test block's output with only a comment ('it should return the same as this is the utc time') to justify it, making it a mirror of the pre-existing expected values rather than a derivation from the +6:00 timezone spec — it verifies the implementation's output equals the UTC-case output without any case where the timezone change should alter the result, so it cannot distinguish a correct offset conversion from a no-op (offset === 0) implementation. If the offset computation in packages/lib/slots.ts silently degrades to always computing offset 0 (e.g. both utcOffset() calls resolving to the same zone), this test still passes, so the exact regression it was written to guard against is the one it cannot detect; a companion case with a non-mirrored expected output (organizer timezone differing from invitee such that the wall-clock times shift) is needed.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from the slot's start instead of its end: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. `end` is always identical to `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test never evaluates the slot's actual end; a slot that starts within working hours but ends past `workingHour.endTime` is returned as available, letting users book past the host's working hours.

[BUG] The new working-hours re-check compares the slot's UTC minutes (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` where slotStartTime = time.utc()) against `workingHour.startTime`/`workingHour.endTime`, which are organizer-local minutes. For any organizer not in UTC, the comparison is shifted by the organizer's UTC offset: e.g. a UTC+6 host with working hours 09:00–17:00 local has workingHour values 540–1020, while slot minutes are UTC 03:00–11:00 (180–660), so nearly every slot fails `start < workingHour.startTime` and getSchedule returns zero bookable slots.

[BUG] The date-override day match compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` (organizer-local wall time of the override) against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` (slot time in UTC), and `utcOffset` is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` — a sign inversion (utcOffset() is already minutes-to-add-to-UTC), so the override instant is shifted away from organizer local time by twice the offset. For a UTC+6 organizer (utcOffset()=360), the code subtracts 360 minutes, producing UTC−6 wall time, then compares it to a UTC slot date; the wrong calendar day is matched for any override whose window crosses the organizer's midnight, blocking the wrong day's slots and leaving the override day's off-hours slots marked available.

[BUG] checkIfIsAvailable is called with `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone`, but `schedule` is the per-timezone schedule built from the invitee's requested timeZone, not the organizer's. When the invitee queries in a different timezone than the organizer, the date-override day computation in checkIfIsAvailable uses the invitee's offset, shifting the override date window by the difference between the two timezones and marking slots on the wrong day as unavailable/available; the same defect is repeated at line ~517 with `userSchedule.timeZone` and line ~579 with `userSchedule?.timeZone`.

[BUG] The organizer offset is derived via `dayjs(override.start.toString())`, reparsing the output of Date.toString() (which renders the instant in the server's local timezone with a locale-dependent "GMT+X (TZ name)" suffix) instead of using the instant directly. dayjs parses the "... GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)" token unreliably, so for any server timezone whose toString() format dayjs mishandles, `organizerUtcOffset` is computed from a misparsed wall time and the entire shift `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` is wrong, silently unsetting the wrong minutes of working hours; it also drops millisecond precision, so DST-offset overrides landing exactly on a transition get the pre- or post-transition offset arbitrarily.

[BUG] After shifting an override by the organizer↔invitee offset, `startTime`/`endTime` are taken as `.hour()*60 + .minute()` with no day-carry, so an override that crosses 00:00 UTC after the shift wraps into 0–1440 minutes of the wrong day. An override like 20:00–23:30 UTC viewed by a +6 invitee shifts to 02:00–05:30 correctly, but one shifting from 22:00 UTC to 04:00 next-day produces startTime=1320 with endTime wrapping to 300, so the working-hours-unset loop clears minutes 1320–1440 plus 0–300 while the interval 300–1320 that should have been cleared stays set — hours the organizer marked unavailable are offered as bookable.

[ADVISORY] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs instances by reference, so it is always false and the intended all-day-blocked (start === end) branch is dead code. The behavior currently happens to be rescued by the surrounding before/after comparisons, so no user is bitten today, but the next editor who reorders or relaxes those comparisons will rely on a check that can never fire and all-day "blocked" overrides will silently leak slots.

[ADVISORY] The round-robin branch resolves the user via `userAvailability.find(...)` after filtering and uses `userSchedule?.timeZone` with no fallback, so a slot whose userId is not present in userAvailability (e.g. filtered out by the preceding currentSeats/busy pre-checks) passes `organizerTimeZone: undefined`. checkIfIsAvailable then treats the organizer as UTC (`organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0`), so date-override day matching for that user's slots silently uses the wrong offset; callers get slots whose override filtering was computed against UTC rather than the host's timezone.

[BUG] The full-day-override branch compares two Dayjs wrapper objects with strict equality (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which is always false since Dayjs returns a new object per call. Full-day date overrides (start === end) are never detected as such; instead they fall through to the range checks below, so a full-day-unavailable override that starts before the slot end is still treated as unavailable but the special full-day case the author coded for is dead code — behavior diverges from intent for any override where start equals end, silently.

[BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime` (`const start = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so the slot's end time is never validated against workingHour.endTime. A slot that starts within working hours but extends past closing time passes the availability check (only `end > workingHour.endTime` would have caught it, but `end` equals the start), so users are offered slots that overrun the host's working hours — a booking can be made for times the host is not working.

[BUG] `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` is passed to checkIfIsAvailable, but `schedule` at this point is the aggregated per-slot schedule value spread from `...schedule` (a Schedule = TimeRange[][] structure with no `timeZone` property per its type in packages/types/schedule.d.ts where timeZone lives on TimeRange entries, not the schedule object), so `schedule.timeZone` is always undefined. checkIfIsAvailable's date-override day-boundary logic falls back to `utcOffset = 0` (UTC) for every slot on this path, so for any organizer outside UTC the override day comparison uses the wrong day — slots on the organizer's override day are wrongly blocked or wrongly allowed depending on offset direction, producing incorrect availability output.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with strict identity, which is always false. The intended zero-length/unavailable-all-day override branch never executes; a date override whose start equals its end is treated as a normal range and the day-level 'dateOverrideExist' fallthrough at line 116 wrongly returns true (available) for every slot that day, exposing slots the organizer explicitly marked unavailable.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called on a field the type declares as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and no producer of the `activeOverrides` passed into `getSlots` is shown to populate it, so `dayjs().tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's local timezone. When `override.timeZone` is undefined, `organizerUtcOffset` becomes the server machine's UTC offset instead of the organizer's, producing a wrong `offset` and thus wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes that unsets the wrong working-hours rows — availability is corrupted for any getSlots call site that doesn't thread timeZone through (the diff only adds timeZone on the dateOverrides in viewer/slots.ts getSchedule, a different object graph).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic unconditionally does `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` but `timeZone` is declared optional on `TimeRange` (`timeZone?: string` in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`). The diff adds `timeZone` only when building `dateOverrides` inside `viewer/slots.ts:getSchedule`, but `getSlots` operates on `activeOverrides` (not shown here) and has no fallback/guard if `override.timeZone` is missing. If it’s undefined at runtime, `tz(undefined)` will use a non-organizer timezone (commonly server local), producing a wrong `offset` and thus wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes when unsetting working hours.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `userSchedule?.timeZone` yields `undefined` when the slot's `slotUserId` has no matching entry in `userAvailability`, and `checkIfIsAvailable` then takes the `organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0` branch, computing a zero utcOffset. For round-robin slots whose userId isn't found in `userAvailability`, the date-override day comparison uses `format("YYYY MM DD")` on the raw UTC instant, matching the override to the wrong calendar day and filtering slots in/out incorrectly across timezone boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: In the round-robin branch, the code derives `organizerTimeZone` via `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(...); organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` (so it can be `undefined` if no match is found). In `checkIfIsAvailable`, an `undefined` `organizerTimeZone` causes the date-override offset to fall back to `0` (`organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0`), which could make the override-day comparison run in raw UTC and potentially mis-evaluate overrides across timezone boundaries. However, the diff does not prove that `slotUserId` can ever be missing from `userAvailability` (it may be guaranteed by upstream construction of `slot.userIds`), so this is an edge-case/robustness concern rather than a demonstrably broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is inside the override window, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before reaching the busy-events check, so conflicts are never consulted. A user who has a confirmed booking or calendar-busy event that overlaps the override window still sees those slots as bookable in getSchedule, and can book a double-booking; the busy.every() conflict logic below is silently skipped for every overridden day.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after detecting a date override on the same day (`dateOverrideExist = true` inside the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback), the function returns `true` immediately when the slot is *within* the override window (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`). This happens before the final `return busy.every(...)` conflict check, so busy events/bookings are never consulted for those overridden-day slots. The `find(...)` is only used to return `false` when the slot is outside the override window; when inside, `find` returns no match but `dateOverrideExist` still triggers the early `true`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime (identical to `start`) instead of the slot's end time, and drops seconds, so it reads `const start = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. A slot that starts at 16:45 with a 30-minute event length passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test even though it ends at 17:15 past a 17:00 working-hours end, so getSchedule returns slots that extend beyond working hours; the check can never test anything start doesn't already test.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs wrapper objects with strict equality, which is always false. The zero-length-override early-return branch is dead code, so a zero-length (unavailable/blocked) date override falls through to the time comparisons and can be treated as an available window instead of a block, exposing slots the organizer explicitly blocked.

[BUG] The override comparison mixes clock domains: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` yields the organizer's local wall time while `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime` are UTC wall times, so the two sides differ by the organizer's UTC offset for any non-UTC organizer. For an organizer in +5:30, an override stored as 18:00–22:00 UTC is compared against slots as if it were 12:30–17:00 UTC; slots are wrongly excluded from and wrongly included in the override window, so the PR's own timezone-fix goal fails for every non-UTC organizer.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime` are explicitly converted to UTC (`time.utc()` / `.add(...).utc()`), but date overrides are transformed via `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` where `utcOffset` is derived from `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`. This shifts the override instants by the organizer’s offset and then compares them against UTC slot instants/dates (`format("YYYY MM DD")`, `isBefore`, `isSame`, `isAfter`). If `date.start`/`date.end` are already real instants (they are `Date`s), applying an additional offset will move the window in UTC and can exclude/include the wrong slots for non-UTC organizers, matching the finding’s described failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new offset math computes minutes-of-day via `.hour()*60 + .minute()` after shifting by the invitee offset, so an override that crosses midnight in the invitee's timezone produces startTime/endTime values outside 0–1439 (or wrapped), which the downstream unset loop matching overrides against working-hours minute ranges cannot handle. An organizer override of 22:00–02:00 viewed by an invitee 6 hours ahead becomes a 04:00–08:00 window computed on the wrong day, and working hours for the intended day are unset based on the wrong date, producing wrong availability for multi-day windows around the override.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override minute-of-day computation uses `dayjs(...).hour()*60 + ...minute()`, which is always in the 0–1439 range (hours 0–23), so it does not produce “values outside 0–1439”. The finding’s core claim about out-of-range/wrap and downstream unset-loop inability is not supported by the diff. While cross-midnight/overnight overrides may have other edge cases (e.g., `endTime < startTime`), that behavior already existed with the previous `getUTCHours()/getUTCMinutes()` approach and the diff doesn’t show the downstream logic needed to verify the claimed multi-day/day-mismatch failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` dereferences `override.timeZone`, which the diff itself types as optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts (`timeZone?: string`), and serializes a Date through toString() before re-parsing. Any producer of TimeRange/dateOverrides that does not populate timeZone (the type contract permits it) gets `dayjs.tz(undefined)` — the current instant — so the offset is computed for 'now' rather than the override date, silently mis-shifting DST-sensitive overrides; a future maintainer cannot tell which producers guarantee the field.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes `organizerUtcOffset` via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `timeZone` was made optional on `TimeRange` (`timeZone?: string` in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`) and there is no guard/fallback if it is missing. The diff also shows unnecessary `Date -> toString() -> parse` round-tripping, which can change parsing semantics. However, in the only producer shown in this diff (`getSchedule`), `dateOverrides` are explicitly enriched with `timeZone: availability.timeZone`, so the claim that `override.timeZone` will be absent (and that `tz(undefined)` will compute an offset for “now”) is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff exercises the getSchedule happy path for one extra invitee timezone, while the entirely new logic in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable (dateOverrideExist gating, the working-hours check, the organizerTimeZone shift) has no test anywhere in the diff. A regression in checkIfIsAvailable — such as the end-time and busy-check defects present in this very diff — ships undetected; the next change to slot filtering has no safety net, and reviewers cannot verify the new working-hours branch behaves correctly for any timezone or busy-overlap case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new filtering logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (date-override gating and a new working-hours exclusion path, plus timezone-offset handling via `organizerTimeZone`), but the only added test (`apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts`) asserts a single additional schedule result for one invitee timezone scenario and does not specifically exercise/validate the new branches in `checkIfIsAvailable` (e.g., working-hours exclusion, override boundary cases, busy-overlap interactions). While the new test may indirectly pass through some of this code via `getSchedule`, the finding’s core point—lack of targeted coverage for the new nontrivial branches—is diff-grounded and actionable as a review concern rather than a guaranteed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new working-hours check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime`, so the working-hours end bound is never enforced. `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` should derive from `slotEndTime`; any slot that starts before `workingHour.endTime` but runs past close of business is returned as available, e.g. a 60-minute event whose slot starts at 16:30 against a 17:00 end is offered even though it ends at 17:30.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object identity of two distinct Dayjs instances, so it is always false. The intended zero-length-override short-circuit (treat override as full-day/unblock) never fires; a zero-length date override that should make the day available instead falls through to the start/end comparisons, where `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` returns true and the day is silently filtered out — the exact opposite of the intended behavior.

[BUG] The organizer offset is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, which both parses a Date with tz() incorrectly and inverts the sign of utcOffset. `dayjs.tz(dateObj, tz)` re-interprets the Date's local wall time in `organizerTimeZone` rather than converting it, and then multiplying `utcOffset()` by -1 flips the offset direction; for any organizer east of UTC the override's calendar day comparison `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format(...)` matches the wrong day, so date overrides block or free the wrong dates for non-UTC organizers.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the diff introduces `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` and then shifts the override boundaries with `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` / `dayjs(date.end)...` before comparing calendar days to `slotStartTime` (which is `time.utc()`). `utcOffset()` is already the minutes offset from UTC for that timezone (positive east of UTC), so multiplying by `-1` and then adding that value shifts dates in the opposite direction, making the day-matching logic likely incorrect for non-UTC organizers (notably timezones east of UTC). This can cause overrides to be applied to the wrong UTC day and incorrectly block/allow slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable re-implements date-override and working-hours filtering from scratch, duplicating the existing enforcement in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots, and the two implementations already disagree in mechanism (slots.ts shifts override times by the invitee-vs-organizer offset; this code shifts by an inverted organizer offset and compares formatted day strings). There are now two hand-maintained sources of truth for the same availability invariant on the same request path; the next maintainer changing override semantics must update both or slots produced by getSlots will be silently filtered differently by checkIfIsAvailable — the divergence is already present in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces new date-override and working-hours filtering inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts, added blocks using `dateOverrides` and `workingHours`), while `packages/lib/slots.ts#getSlots` already applies date overrides by unsetting working hours (and was just modified to shift override times by an invitee-vs-organizer offset). These are two separate implementations of the same availability constraints, and they do use different mechanisms (e.g., `getSlots` computes `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, while `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and compares formatted day strings). This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/consistency risk (two sources of truth) rather than a single directly provable functional break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The override-window checks reject a slot only if `slotEndTime` is at/before the override start or `slotStartTime` is after the override end, but accept slots that straddle the override boundary (start before the override begins, end inside it), and since `dateOverrideExist` then returns true unconditionally, such slots bypass working-hours checks entirely. A slot overlapping the edge of a date override (e.g. starting 30 minutes before the override window) is returned as available even though part of the booking falls outside the override's permitted window and outside normal working hours.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once any `dateOverride` exists for the same UTC day (`dateOverrideExist = true` inside the `find` callback), the function returns `true` unconditionally (`if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`) unless the `find` returns a truthy value that triggers `return false` (which only happens when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, i.e., clearly outside). For a slot that *straddles* the override start (starts before `date.start` but ends after it), neither outside-condition matches, so it bypasses the `return false` and then hits `return true`, allowing availability even though part of the slot is outside the override window and skipping the later working-hours (and busy) checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff hoists `organizerTimeZone` computation out of the loop and then, for round-robin/collective hosts, overrides it per-user via `userSchedule?.timeZone`, but for fixed events passes `schedule.timeZone` — the availability check receives a timezone whose semantics differ per code path with no single traceable requirement for which one governs. A future change to how eventType-level vs user-level timezones resolve (e.g. schedule-less event types) will produce different override filtering for fixed vs round-robin event types from the same PR-added code, and maintainers must reason about three assignment sites (lines ~439, ~492, ~517, ~579) to change it safely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple, differing sources passed as `organizerTimeZone` into `checkIfIsAvailable`: a hoisted fallback (`eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone`) used in `getAvailableUserSchedules`, but then per-slot availability checks pass `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` (fixed path) and `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` (round-robin/collective paths) at several call sites. Since `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `organizerTimeZone` to shift `dateOverrides` comparisons, this creates a maintainability/semantic ambiguity grounded in the diff (multiple assignment sites with different meaning), even if it’s not provably incorrect without broader requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the new workingHours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `end` is computed from slotStartTime (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) instead of slotEndTime, so start === end and the `end > workingHour.endTime` test degenerates to a start-time comparison. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past workingHour.endTime is wrongly marked available — e.g. a 60-minute slot at 16:30 against a 17:00 working-hours end slips through the availability check and is shown as bookable; the intended `end` must come from slotEndTime.

[BUG] The new workingHours gate compares UTC components of the slot against organizer-local working-hour values: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` so `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + minute()` is UTC minutes, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes in the organizer's timezone, and `slotStartTime.day()` is the UTC weekday while `workingHour.days` holds local weekdays. For any organizer not on UTC (e.g. +6:00 with 09:00-17:00 working hours), the check filters the wrong slots — slots near local boundaries are rejected or admitted incorrectly, and slots on the local Sunday/Saturday boundary are evaluated against the wrong day. This gate also duplicates the working-hours filtering already done in getSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts), creating two parallel filter paths that can disagree.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `slotStartTime = time.utc()` / `slotEndTime = time.add(...).utc()` and then compares `slotStartTime.day()` and `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` against `workingHour.days/startTime/endTime` (which are working-hours values, not shown here, but clearly not derived from UTC in this function). There is no timezone conversion for the slot before the comparison, so for non-UTC organizers/invitees this will evaluate the wrong weekday and minute-of-day. Additionally, the code computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute();` (same as `start`), so it never accounts for the event length when checking `end > workingHour.endTime`, which is a concrete correctness defect visible in the diff. This logic can therefore incorrectly reject/admit slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The full-day-override test `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs wrapper objects with strict reference equality, which is always false. The full-day (start==end) date-override branch is dead code and never fires; the code falls through to the before/after checks instead, which for a start==end override reject every slot that isn't strictly after the override instant — i.e. full-day overrides behave as point overrides and slots that should be available are marked unavailable (or vice versa) depending on the subsequent branches.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new full-day/zero-length override check uses strict reference equality between two distinct Dayjs instances: `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )`. This can never be true because each `dayjs()` call returns a new wrapper object, so that branch is dead code. For overrides where `start` and `end` are equal, the logic then falls through to the before/after comparisons (e.g., `slotEndTime.isBefore(...) || slotEndTime.isSame(...)`), which will treat such overrides as a point-in-time boundary and can incorrectly reject/allow slots. This defect is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The offset correction shifts only the time-of-day of each override (`dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`) while the day-matching loop immediately below still keys off the original, unshifted override window, so when the offset pushes the override across midnight (offsets > the override's distance from 00:00) the shifted startTime is larger than endTime and the unset loop subtracts shifted times against an unshifted day. For organizer/invitee timezone pairs whose offset crosses a midnight boundary (e.g. organizer at +6:00 with an 00:00-08:00 override viewed from UTC-8), the computed startTime > endTime and the working-hours-unset loop removes the wrong (or no) hours, producing slots outside the override window or hiding the override entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` purely as minutes-of-day after applying an offset (`dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`). This drops the date component, so if the offset pushes the override across midnight, the minutes-of-day can wrap and yield `startTime > endTime`. The subsequent override application loop ("unset all working hours...") operates on these minute ranges and (as typical for such logic) will mis-handle inverted ranges, effectively removing the wrong hours or none at all. The diff shows no normalization/splitting for cross-midnight overrides, so the reported midnight-boundary issue is a real correctness risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the newly-optional `timeZone` field on TimeRange; any caller building dateOverrides without setting timeZone (the field was just made optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts) passes undefined into dayjs.tz, and the offset then defaults to the host machine's timezone rather than failing loudly. Server operators on hosts whose local tz differs from the organizer's get silently wrong override windows; the field should be required or the missing case should throw rather than degrade to server-local offsets.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes `organizerUtcOffset` via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` makes `TimeRange.timeZone` optional (`timeZone?: string`). There is no guard or fallback in `getSlots` if `override.timeZone` is `undefined`, so callers that build `activeOverrides` without `timeZone` will pass an undefined timezone into `dayjs.tz(...)`, leading to incorrect offset calculations (or non-obvious default behavior) and therefore incorrect override windows. This is a correctness defect in the diff because the code path assumes a value that the type explicitly allows to be missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `organizerTimeZone` fallback chain ends with `userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone`, i.e. the timezone of whichever availability record happened to be first, not necessarily the organizer's. When eventType.timeZone and schedule.timeZone are unset (collective/round-robin setups), availability math silently keys off an arbitrary member's timezone; results shift per query depending on Prisma row order.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does define `organizerTimeZone` as `eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), so the fallback can indeed depend on whichever `userAvailability` entry is first when the event/schedule timezone is unset. However, this fallback chain already existed in the pre-change code path (it was previously passed inline to `getTimeSlots`), and the PR also starts passing per-user `schedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule?.timeZone` into `checkIfIsAvailable`, which mitigates some availability checks. The finding is a valid, diff-grounded concern about ambiguity in collective setups, but the claim about results shifting per Prisma row order is not directly verifiable from the diff alone, and it’s not clearly a newly introduced breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In the round-robin branch, `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(...)` can return undefined (userId not found among availability), and `userSchedule?.timeZone` then yields undefined organizerTimeZone, which checkIfIsAvailable treats as utcOffset 0 instead of the real organizer offset. For a slot userId missing from userAvailability, the date-override date comparison silently runs as if the organizer were on UTC, admitting/rejecting slots against the wrong day.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the round-robin filtering path does `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(...)` and then passes `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` into `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts). If the `find` misses, `organizerTimeZone` becomes `undefined`, and `checkIfIsAvailable` explicitly falls back to `utcOffset = 0` when `organizerTimeZone` is falsy. That could lead to date-override comparisons being done as if the organizer were in UTC. However, from this diff alone it’s not verifiable that `slotUserId` can ever be absent from `userAvailability` (it may be guaranteed by how `timeSlots`/`slot.userIds` are constructed elsewhere), so this is a defensiveness/edge-case concern rather than a clearly reproducible defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` is recomputed twice per boundary (four dayjs constructions per override) instead of computing the shifted start/end once. Pure wasted allocation on the hot slots path with no behavior benefit; a single `const shiftedStart = ...; const shiftedEnd = ...` halves the work and removes the risk of the four copies drifting apart.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override mapping computes `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` twice for `startTime` (once for `.hour()` and again for `.minute()`), and similarly computes `dayjs(override.end)...` twice for `endTime`. This is diff-grounded redundant work/allocation that can be avoided by storing shifted start/end in locals; it's a performance/cleanliness concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a slot falls inside a date override's day and passes the range checks, `dateOverrideExist` causes `checkIfIsAvailable` to `return true` before the `busy.every(...)` check ever runs. Slots during a date override are offered even when the host has a confirmed booking or busy block overlapping them, so users can book double-booked times — the function's original purpose (busy filtering) is silently bypassed whenever an override exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the newly added date-override logic can short-circuit before the busy check. When a slot is on a day that has a matching override (`dateOverrideExist = true`) and the `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate does *not* return `true` (i.e., the slot is considered within the override range), the function immediately executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and never reaches `return busy.every(...)`. This means any slot deemed valid due to a date override bypasses conflict filtering (`busy.every`), allowing slots to be offered even if they overlap `busy` intervals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — identical to `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never fire, so slots that start inside working hours but extend past closing time (e.g. a 60-min slot at 16:45 with endTime 17:00) are accepted as available and bookable past the host's working window.

[BUG] The working-hours comparison mixes UTC slot minutes with organizer-local working-hour minutes: `slotStartTime` is `.utc()` (per line `const slotStartTime = time.utc();`) while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes-from-midnight in the organizer's timezone, with no offset applied. For any host whose timezone is not UTC, valid slots inside working hours are rejected and slots outside working hours are accepted — availability is shifted by the host's UTC offset.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the code sets `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then checks working hours via `const start = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` against `workingHour.startTime/endTime` without applying `organizerTimeZone` or any offset. Since `workingHour.*` are minutes-from-midnight in the organizer’s local schedule, this compares UTC minutes to local minutes and will shift availability for non-UTC organizers. The diff shows `organizerTimeZone` is passed in but not used in the working-hours block, confirming the mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two Dayjs object instances by reference, which is always false regardless of values. The intended zero-length-override case is never detected, so a zero-length/unavailability override never short-circuits the range logic as designed; the branch is dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override logic contains `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { return true; }`. Each `dayjs(...)` call creates a new Dayjs instance, so `===` compares object references and will always be false even when the underlying timestamps are equal.
